title: [Performance][v0.32.0rc] Optimize A2/A3 INT8 QSFA no-RoPE computation and KV gather
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #20456 to `releases/v0.32.0rc`.

The six modified arch22 operator files are byte-for-byte identical to the implementation in #20456. The release branch's existing arch35 changes are preserved. A local merge-tree check confirms that integrating this branch into release base `a26cc45a` produces exactly the prepared release-port source tree, with no changes outside the intended operator files and the release note.

Optimize the arch22 INT8 per-tile implementation of `KvQuantSparseFlashAttentionVllm` on A2/A3. The existing no-RoPE path reserves and computes an internal 576-wide attention dimension; this port computes the actual 512 dimensions and reduces sparse KV preparation overhead.

The kernel implementation is ported from CANN ops-transformer PR [!14492](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-transformer/pull/14492), with adaptive address-cache commit [157a925c](https://gitcode.com/mufei_L/ops-transformer/commit/157a925c6282f54bb8707cac5dd63f42a210b3c9) and valid-prefix commit [9668a6d7](https://gitcode.com/mufei_L/ops-transformer/commit/9668a6d7b2236bbc6928a4ff7d239c26e91b250c).

- Specialize arch22 no-RoPE matrix computation to 512 dimensions and perform KV ND2NZ during Cube loading, retaining the existing workspace slot stride.
- Hoist invariant gather parameters, combine eligible KV transfers, and reuse three UB staging slots.
- Cache page-table entries and prepare sparse physical row addresses in batches. Use bounded address storage and S2 segments when a whole query does not fit.
- Preserve address caching for the valid prefix of sparse-index rows ending in `-1` in the adaptive large-table/large-K path.
- Limit idle arch22 launches for short query inputs.

Scope: FP16/BF16 query, INT8 per-tile key/value (`key_quant_mode=value_quant_mode=2`, `quant_scale_repo_mode=1`, `tile_size=128`), with RoPE dimension 0 or 64. The public operator schema, softmax outputs, and existing tiling-key ABI are preserved. Arch35 files are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: lower operator latency within the existing supported contract. There are no new user arguments or environment variables. A performance release-note fragment is included in this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

The hardware results below are carried over from #20456; they are not a new execution of this release-branch checkout. The backported arch22 operator files are identical. This backport passed `git diff --check`, codespell, and source/merge-tree equality checks. Release-branch CI and hardware integration remain to be completed.

Hardware and environment: Ascend A3, CANN 9.2.0 B234, vLLM 0.32.0.

The A3 validation compares PR base `cae7ff02` with head `3b76b647`. Native operators were compiled separately from each revision, without additional modifications to operator or framework source code. The subsequent co-author commit-message update does not change either source tree.

#### Operator correctness and real-input replay

- Ran the repository QSFA tests on a single A3 device: **54 passed and 24 A5-only cases skipped for each version**.
- Replayed an actual full-model tensor dump without modifying the inputs: Query `[16384,8,512]`, BF16 Query, INT8 KV, no RoPE, and no LSE output. Each version was checked in three rounds; all outputs matched the full-model reference element by element.

#### Full-model performance

Model: GLM-5.3-Flash-W8A8, MRv2, INT8 KV, `max-model-len=135168`. AISBench used fixed concurrency 200 and 400 requests per group. Each version ran three rounds.

**Prefill-only (P)**

DP2/TP8, one output token, `max-num-batched-tokens=16384`, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` enabled.

- **4K input, 0% prefix-cache hit rate:** average TTFT decreased **5.04%**; request throughput and input-token throughput each increased **5.27%**.
- **128K input, approximately 89.71% prefix-cache hit rate:** average TTFT decreased **2.13%**; request throughput and input-token throughput each increased **2.13%**.

**Decode-only (D)**

DP4/TP4, concurrency 50 per rank, 1024 output tokens, `max-num-batched-tokens=192`, and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` enabled.

- Actual input lengths were **4353 / 130561 tokens** for the 4K / 128K scenarios, respectively. Local prefix-cache hit rates were **99.977% / 99.999%**.
- **Neither scenario showed a performance gain.**

Earlier A2 validation also covered boundary cases and NaN/Inf initialization: 129 legal supplemental configurations and 387 GM-poison variants passed. These results supplement the A3 repository tests and actual-input replay above.

Known scope: this PR does not add test files or change the public operator contract. Tables of width <=256 with K<=2560 retain the CANN small-table address-preparation path, where tail `-1` may disable address caching; no universal performance gain is claimed for every input.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage reviewed and validated on hardware as detailed above.
- [ ] Regression test added (no operator contract change; focused external hardware validation used).
- [x] Error / failure path coverage, including expected unsupported-head rejection and empty inputs.
- [x] Meaningful & reliable tests: independent references and complete-output comparisons.
- [x] Performance impact: matched-workload A3 full-model prefill/decode comparisons recorded above.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
